what: A semantic cache stores past LLM answers and reuses one when a new question means the same thing, even if the words differ. It compares embeddings (number vectors of meaning) instead of exact text.
like: Like a help desk that keeps answered tickets: 'how do I reset my password' and 'forgot my password' get the same reply without asking an expert again.
why: Cuts LLM cost for repeated questions
Answers in milliseconds instead of seconds
Takes load off rate-limited model providers

nodes.t: LLM provider|has its own prefix cache

steps.d: The gateway hashes the normalised prompt plus model, settings and tenant. An identical repeat returns the stored answer at once - the cheapest possible hit.
On an exact miss, an embedding model turns the question into a vector, so questions with the same meaning land close together.
Search the vector index, filtered by tenant or user. If the closest stored question is within the distance threshold, return its answer: a semantic hit.
Otherwise call the LLM, then store the question vector and answer. The provider's prefix cache separately discounts the repeated start of the prompt.
Each entry carries a TTL (time to live). Short TTLs for news or prices, longer for stable facts; clear entries when the source data changes.
Track exact hit rate, semantic hit rate and the false-hit rate from sampled reviews, so you know the cache saves money without giving wrong answers.

numbers.l: Redis cosine distance range; 0 means identical
example distance threshold in RedisVL docs; lower is stricter
Claude cache read price vs base input, for most models
default Claude prompt cache lifetime, refreshed free on each use
minimum cacheable prompt for OpenAI GPT-5.6 and later

choices.d: Strict thresholds give few but safe hits; loose ones give more hits and more wrong answers. Tune on labelled pairs of questions marked same or different, per embedding model.
Include tenant, user (for private data), model, system prompt version and language in the key or filter, so one customer never sees another's answer.
Set TTL by how fast the truth changes. Clear or version entries when source documents, prompts or the model change.
Cache stable, general questions. Skip personal, time-sensitive or long multi-turn conversations, where the same words can need different answers.
Exact hash lookup is free of false hits and very cheap. Add semantic lookup behind it only where paraphrased repeats are common.

instead.why: Plain exact-key cache: zero false hits, but only identical prompts match
Cache the retrieved documents or tool results instead of final answers
The store a semantic cache is built on, used for retrieval too
Rely on provider prefix caching alone when every answer must be fresh

breaks.d: 'Cancel my order' matches 'cancel my subscription' and returns the wrong answer.
breaks.see: Thumbs-down or complaints on cached answers; sampled reviews find mismatches
breaks.fix: Stricter threshold tuned on labelled pairs, plus a reranker or quick LLM check on borderline hits

breaks.d: Prices or policies changed but the cache keeps serving the old reply.
breaks.see: Cached answers disagree with the source documents
breaks.fix: Shorter TTLs, invalidate on data change, version keys by document or prompt version

breaks.d: A private answer for one customer is served to another with a similar question.
breaks.see: Audit finds hits where the tenant differs
breaks.fix: Tenant and user filters on every lookup, never cache personal answers globally

breaks.d: Questions are too varied, so the cache costs an embedding call and gives little back.
breaks.see: Semantic hit rate stays in single digits while latency rises
breaks.fix: Cache only high-repeat routes, or rely on exact cache and provider prefix caching

say: In the LLM gateway I'd check an exact hash cache first, then a semantic cache that embeds the question and looks for a neighbour within a distance threshold.
I'd tune that threshold on labelled pairs of same and different questions, because a false hit means a confident wrong answer.
Cache entries are scoped by tenant, model and prompt version, with TTLs matched to how fast the data changes.
Provider prompt caching is separate: it discounts a repeated prompt prefix, so I'd put the stable system prompt and documents first to get both savings.

followups.q: How is semantic caching different from provider prompt caching?
followups.a: Semantic caching skips the model call entirely by reusing a whole answer for a similar question. Prompt caching still calls the model but reuses work on an identical prompt prefix, billed at a discount such as 0.1x for Claude cache reads.

followups.q: How do you pick the similarity threshold?
followups.a: Collect real question pairs, label them same-answer or different-answer, then measure hit rate and false-hit rate at several thresholds. Choose the loosest threshold whose false-hit rate your product accepts, and redo it when the embedding model changes.

followups.q: Which metrics show the cache is working?
followups.a: Exact and semantic hit rate, false-hit rate from sampled human or LLM review, latency on hits versus misses, and money saved per day compared with the cost of embedding calls.

followups.q: Would you cache answers in a multi-turn chat?
followups.a: Usually only the first turn or standalone questions. Later turns depend on earlier context, so the same words can need a different answer. Include a conversation summary in the key if you must.

today: Provider prompt caching kept getting cheaper in 2026: OpenAI lists cached input discounted up to 95%, so teams usually structure prompts for prefix caching first and add a semantic cache only for high-repeat questions.

check.q: 'How do I reset my password?' and 'Forgot my password' should share an answer. Which cache can do that?
check.why: Only embedding similarity sees that different words mean the same thing.

check.q: Cached answers are sometimes for a different question. What do you change?
check.a: Make the distance threshold stricter, tuned on labelled pairs
check.why: A stricter threshold only accepts very close matches, cutting false hits.

check.q: What does provider prompt caching reuse?
check.a: An identical prompt prefix, billed at a discount
check.why: Prefix caching needs an exact match on the start of the prompt and still runs the model.

check.q: Why put the tenant id in every semantic cache lookup?
check.a: So one customer never gets another customer's answer
d: Because vector search needs it to work
check.why: Similar questions from different tenants can need private, different answers.
